V-M-SOUND.Scenario: With sound switched on, each effect the interface asks for is played exactly once.
With sound switched off the service calls the player zero times: silence is the expected outcome here, not a failure.
A press, a route push and a route pop each make their own sound, and the app's first route is excluded because it is not a navigation the user made.
A repeat of the same effect inside the 40 ms window is dropped, so a fast tapper cannot machine-gun clicks.
With music switched on, a track starts when the service loads and the next one follows when the current one finishes, wrapping back to the first at the end of the rotation.
With music switched off the player is never asked to start: silence is the expected outcome, not a failure, and the same holds for the track-completion path.
The music pauses when the app leaves the foreground and returns only while the channel is enabled, so a backgrounded companion is silent.

Two concurrent starts of the same track must yield one player only: asking for a track that is already playing must not restart it. This regressed once and the symptom was one track audible in two voices.
A return to the foreground must not start the track over: resume continues it from the position the pause left, so the listener does not lose their place.
A genuine tap anywhere in the app clicks once through the root interceptor, so a surface added later needs no sound code, and a surface that is not Material ink is covered too.
A drag stays silent on a drag beyond the framework's own tap threshold, however far it travels and even if it returns to where it began: scrolling a list must never click.
Popups sound their own opening and closing, so a popup added later needs no sound code: a sheet or a dialog needs no call, and a page keeps navigate and back while the app's first route stays silent.

The eight effects must be loudness-matched and every one must clear the music bed by at least eight decibels. A flat set of sounds is a failure here, not a matter of taste: the press effect once sat eight decibels BELOW the music and most buttons therefore sounded silent while the player was faithfully playing them.
No effect may ask for a volume the player would clamp, or the arithmetic above it stops describing what is heard.

A press whose release never arrives must not silence the presses that follow: after a lost release one gesture is lost, never every gesture until the app restarts. This regressed once and it made the whole application quiet.

The threshold that separates a tap from a drag is the framework's device-aware one, so the interceptor and the button underneath agree on what a tap is — a mouse press that drifts is not one, while a finger's may be.
